instruction: Change the font of all text in this document to Arial and set the font size to 14.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully set different line spacing (single, double, 1.5) for three paragraphs by selecting each paragraph and using the Paragraph dialog to change Line Spacing settings.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select individual paragraphs in LibreOffice Writer, open Paragraph formatting dialog, and change paragraph-level formatting properties.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests font and size changes, a different formatting operation but using the same select-all + apply pattern. Original was Times New Roman 12pt, now requires Arial 14pt.
metadata.explanation: Custom getter reads font names and sizes from all runs in the docx. Custom metric checks that all text uses Arial font (0.5 credit) and 14pt size (0.5 credit).

llm_judge_reasons: Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule': accesses expected.get('expected_font') and expected.get('expected_size_pt') directly from the rules dict.
Getter correctly extracts font names and sizes from all non-empty runs in the docx, converting EMU to pt (1pt = 12700 EMU).
Metric provides proper partial credit: 0.5 for font match (all runs use Arial) and 0.5 for size match (all runs use 14pt), with reasonable 0.5pt tolerance for size comparison.
Both instruction requirements (font change to Arial + size change to 14) are fully covered by the evaluator.
Postconfig correctly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring docx reflects the agent's changes.

Minor concern: python-docx run.font.name returns only directly-applied font, not inherited from paragraph/document style. If some runs inherit font without explicit run-level setting, the getter may produce incomplete font set. In practice, selecting all text and changing font in LibreOffice typically applies at run level, so this is unlikely to cause issues.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also reading paragraph-level style fonts (paragraph.style.font.name) as a fallback for runs where run.font.name is None, to handle font inheritance edge cases.
